answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity capital stake slashed to zero once a pseudonym is caught colluding. An agent locks a deposit into the protocol vault before its vote counts, and each new identity is sized by a uniqueness test drawing corroboration from unrelated operators, so N lookalikes cost N deposits. Outvoting honest nodes needs a majority of staked capital, forfeited on detection. The kernel is economic: the Nth fake identity's marginal cost stays flat and unrecoverable, and each sign-up burns a quill of irrecoverable stake, so capture costs more than it can win.
